title: Private program ledger (schema v1)
description: A researcher's own transcription of bug-bounty program terms. PRIVATE by design: entries name real programs, so this file is never published. The repository ships the schema, not the data. The top level is a LIST of entries; the version lives in $id and, optionally, in each entry's schema_version. The version matrix (bounty-economics schema version <-> viability-gate ledger version) is documented in README.md.

schema_version.description: Ledger format version this entry is written against. Optional; absent means 1. A validator that does not implement the pinned version must reject the entry rather than mis-read it.

id.description: Your own slug for the program. Stable across rounds.

tier_shape.description: Which severities the program pays. 'unknown' means the reward table has not been transcribed and MUST NOT be read as permissive. A program whose page states no floor at all ('NONE', 'any', or nothing) is ALSO 'unknown' until the reward table is read, because informational findings are acknowledged rather than paid and no floor statement is not evidence that Low pays; record that state in floor_status: unstated. There is deliberately no 'any' value.

floor_status.description: Whether the floor was READ. 'documented' = the reward table was read and its lowest paying tier recorded. 'unstated' = the page states no floor; this is not evidence that Low pays, it is evidence the page has not been read, so tier_shape stays 'unknown'. 'conflicting' = the program's own materials disagree about the floor; record both in 'conflicts'. Strongly recommended: the validator warns when it is absent.

floor_severity.description: Lowest severity with a non-zero reward, and only when floor_status is 'documented'. Null when the floor is unstated or the shape is unknown. 'informational' is not a valid floor: no program pays it in practice.

source_url.description: The live rewards/scope page this was read from. Required: an uncited entry is rejected.

retrieved.description: ISO date the page was read. Required, because program terms change without notice.

conflicts.description: Disagreements found in the program's own materials, e.g. a scope table labelling an asset Critical while the rewards table pays it at High. The rewards table governs; record the conflict rather than resolving it silently.

clause.description: Verbatim from the program's scope page.

pattern.description: Case-insensitive regex to test against your own finding description. A match is a prompt to check, not an automatic reject.

covers.description: Files and functions covered. A report naming a file is not the same as covering your function.

known_issues.description: The program's own known-issues list, verbatim.

post_audit_delta.description: What changed after the last audit. The richest surface, and the least likely to be a duplicate.
